svg.title: The IDE footprint is partly your own extensions
svg.desc: Breakdown of the one IDE surface, Copilot in VS Code, which enabled 56 native tools at the baseline. 38 are core Copilot tools (product default); 18 come from notebook and browser extensions the user installed. The system block also folds in 16 skill blocks and an 8-agent roster, but those are mostly not product defaults: 9 come straight from the workspace repository's .github folder, 8 from user-installed extensions, and only 6 are Copilot built-ins. Git branch and status and workspace metadata are workspace-derived. The export does not expose a clean system-versus-context wire split, so finer attribution is not observable. A large part of the so-called IDE footprint is repository and user-installed configuration, not a product default.
svg.text: An IDE adds a workspace, not just a window
Copilot in VS Code, baseline: 56 native tools split by who put them there.
~16.6k of the 20.6k total is the tool catalog; about a third of those tools are not Copilot's own.
Core Copilot tool schemas (38) — Product default
Notebook + browser extension tools (18) — User-configured (installed extensions)
System instructions + 16 skills / 8 agents — Mostly repo .github + installed extensions — folded into system block
Git branch / status, workspace metadata — Workspace-derived
System-vs-context wire split — Not observable from the export
Source: co-ide-exports/CO-IDE_agent_sonnet_MCPoff.json. The export folds system + skills + context into one block, so dynamic editor state is not separable.
